Subject: Post-call: Trial runbook proposal + evaluation rubric (next steps)

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and a concrete trial proposal so we can get alignment and book the kickoff. I kept this intentionally prescriptive so everyone (internal + PiperTech) knows who owns what and what success looks like.

Key discovery points (from call)
- Primary goal: Replace existing customer message categorization pipeline with lower latency + comparable precision for the high-value labels (fraud, compliance).
- Throughput: ~50 req/s steady during business hours; occasional spikes to 250 req/s.
- Data: You can provide a 10k example set (anonymized) + streaming access to a small traffic shadow stream.
- Security: You’ll ask SRE for the SOC2 checklist and a point-of-contact for host network scanning.

Proposed trial approach (recommended): hands-on runbook (hybrid shadow + focused offline grading)
- Phase A (Warm / Shadow, days 1–4): Route a 5% sampled production stream to Redwood shadow endpoint for live comparison. This lets us validate latency, routing, and KV-cache behavior in real traffic.
- Phase B (Focused offline grading, days 5–9): Run the 10k labeled set and an additional 2k hard negatives through our evaluation harness to compute precision/recall by label and degradation modes.
- Phase C (Acceptance validation, day 10): Short synthetic load test + final scorecard review and decision meeting.

Success criteria (pass/fail gates)
- Primary labels: Precision >= your current system - 1.5% and recall within 3% absolute.
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 350ms for typical payloads.
- Reliability: No more than 1% error rate on shadow traffic; no dropped requests during the synthetic test.
- Cost: Token unit cost not to exceed your target (we'll model this after we see actual request sizes).

Owners & asks
- PiperTech: Please share the anonymized 10k dataset + SRE contact for the security questionnaire (Devon copied). Also confirm who will be the primary trial decision-maker (accept/fail).
- Redwood: Aditya will own the shadow deployment and load-sim; Ben will run the offline grading pipeline and produce the rubric. I’ll coordinate the kickoff, docs, and final decision meeting.

Next steps (short list)
1) PiperTech: Share dataset link + SRE contact by Fri 11 Jun.
2) Redwood: We prepare the trial runbook and rubric (attached: trial-runbook-draft.pdf, evaluation-rubric-v1.xlsx) and share updated version by Mon 14 Jun.
3) Schedule 30-min kickoff (proposed window next Tue/Wed) — calendar link in related links.

Attachments: trial-runbook-draft.pdf (outline of play-by-play), evaluation-rubric-v1.xlsx (label-level scoring), piper-data-sample-README.txt (format expectations).

Thanks — Mina

Sara — thanks, and good question on data. Short answers + a recommended fallback:
- Preferred: anonymized original text + label. Our grading tools compute label-level confusion matrices and inspect context windows — feature vectors reduce our ability to debug edge cases.
- If PiperTech policy prevents full text sharing: provide 1) hashed tokens or 2) an extraction of only the relevant fields (e.g., message_type, label, timestamp) plus a small sample of raw text (500 rows) for debugging.

Operational note on shadowing: we'll do an initial 24–48 hour warmup with sampling at 1% to validate routing and metrics collection before moving to 5% sample. That mitigates risk and gives you a safe on-ramp. For the synthetic acceptance test, we'll run a 30-minute p95-focused load that mirrors peak payload sizes.

Ben and I will take point on the rubric — Ben will share a populated scoring sheet by Mon with sample calculations for the primary labels so you can see how the pass/fail gates are computed.

Aditya
